intuition: Use each array position to mark whether its corresponding value appears. When you see value v, make position v - 1 negative. Repeated values leave the marker negative. After the scan, a positive position means its corresponding number was never seen.

When value v appears, make the value at index v-1 negative. A previously marked input position may later be read as part of the scan, so recover its original magnitude with abs before deriving its home index. Repeated appearances must leave the marker negative; toggling the sign would wrongly erase evidence of an even number of copies.

After all values have marked their homes, scan the positions again. A positive entry means its corresponding number never appeared; append index+1 to the result. The magnitude stored at that home is irrelevant to this second pass: its sign alone is the presence flag.
The method relies on strictly positive original values and the bounded value range, which guarantee both unambiguous signs and valid home indices.

intuition: Comparing every value from one through array length against the whole input is quadratic. Each allowed value can instead leave a presence mark at its corresponding address.

concept.observation: Presence marks are permanent; repeats must not erase them.
approach: Mark the address belonging to each scanned magnitude.

concept.correctness: Marking preserves every original magnitude and makes address v−1 negative exactly when v occurs. Repeating a value leaves that invariant unchanged. Thus after the scan a positive address is equivalent to absence of its represented value, and reading all such addresses produces every missing value once.
